page: ALCAR (Acetyl-L-carnitine) — Dose, Form and Timing
section: Dose Range (property); also the 2026-09-24 Evidence revision ('the one skin-biopsy study … found no change')
sentence_as_it_stands: 3,000 mg/day showed no significant morphometric difference and, in the one skin-biopsy study, no change in intraepidermal fibre density. No human study has shown small-fibre regrowth at any dose.
quote: Highly significant increases occurred in both epidermal (mean 100%; P = 0.006) and dermal (mean 133%; P < 0.0001) innervation after 6 months of ALCAR treatment
corrected_wording: 3,000 mg/day showed no significant morphometric difference. Two skin-biopsy studies exist, both uncontrolled HIV-neuropathy cohorts at 3,000 mg/day: one counted intraepidermal fibres and found no change (Valcour 2009); the other measured immunostaining area and reported increases in epidermal and dermal small sensory fibres (Hart 2004). No controlled human study has shown small-fibre regrowth at any dose.
notes: Hart 2004 is an open cohort (n=21, 16 re-biopsied at six months), the same design class as Valcour's open-label pilot. Its result cannot establish regrowth without a control arm, but it is a second skin-biopsy study, and a positive one.

page: 🕳️ What was searched for and does not exist, so it is not searched for again
section: The things this page says do not exist > item 5, the field-size argument
sentence_as_it_stands: The largest published intradermal field is both feet: 141 patients, [dose figure omitted] with an insulin syringe, [dose figure omitted] in the group treated bilaterally
quote: For each patient, total of [dose figure omitted] of BTX- A was injected.
corrected_wording: The largest published intradermal field is both feet: 141 patients in three randomised arms — one foot treated with saline into the other, both feet treated, and saline into both feet. The trial gave each patient the same total amount in both active arms and divided it equally between the two feet in the bilateral arm, so treating both feet halved the amount per foot rather than doubling the total. Scaling this trial to a larger field has to start from the per-patient total, not from a per-foot figure doubled.
notes: The paper states the per-patient total explicitly and says the total injected volume per patient was equal in all three arms (p. 2); the bilateral arm's per-foot share is half the unilateral arm's. The figures the page gives for the bilateral group are therefore the per-foot amount of the other arm and a total the trial never used. The arithmetic sentence that follows this one in the page scales that doubled total to both legs, so the correction changes its starting point; the page's own conclusion that no trial has treated a field as large as both entire legs is unaffected. Figures omitted here under the dose rule; they are in the paper card and in the C008 update's reason.

page: 🕳️ What was searched for and does not exist, so it is not searched for again
section: Sources > S18 (Taheri 2020)
sentence_as_it_stands: 141 patients in three arms; [dose figure omitted], [dose figure omitted] with an insulin syringe; VAS and every Neuropathy Pain Scale item improved against placebo except dull sensation (p=0.114) and cold sensation (p=0.653).
quote: For each patient, total of [dose figure omitted] of BTX- A was injected.
corrected_wording: 141 patients, 47 per arm, in three arms: toxin into one foot with saline into the other, the same per-patient total divided between both feet, and saline into both feet. The amount is a per-patient total, not a per-foot dose; the bilateral arm's per-foot share is half the unilateral arm's. Injected intradermally with an insulin needle on a fixed grid over the sole of the foot. VAS and every Neuropathy Pain Scale item improved against placebo except dull sensation (p=0.114) and cold sensation (p=0.653); the two active arms differed on hot sensation only (p=0.003), which improved less when the amount was divided between both feet.
notes: The per-foot figure describes the unilateral arm only, and reading it as the bilateral arm's dose is what produces the doubled total in the body of the page. Also worth adding: the grid was on the sole, which this entry does not say, and which the botulinum page has right.

page: 🕳️ What was searched for and does not exist, so it is not searched for again
section: Sources > S18 (Taheri 2020), Limits
sentence_as_it_stands: this is the largest intradermal field ever published and it is both feet, which is the fact this page cites; single centre in Tehran; per-arm numbers, confidence intervals and the exact toxin preparation are not given in the abstract; the design mixes a within-patient comparison (one foot against the other) with a between-patient one, and the two are reported together.
quote: In our study, patients who received unilateral BTX-A injections showed decreased VAS score in both feet, which may reflect the central effects of BTX-A injection (and not just the topical effect).
corrected_wording: this is the largest intradermal field ever published and it is both feet, which is the fact this page cites; single centre in Tehran; the design mixes a within-patient comparison (one foot against the other) with a between-patient one, and only the between-patient comparisons are reported — pain was scored per patient, never per foot, so the saline-injected foot has no result of its own and the authors' statement that relief appeared in both feet is an impression in the discussion, with no count behind it. From the full text: 47 patients per arm; the preparation and grid are given; outcomes were measured at four weeks, although the design sentence says three months of follow-up; every patient also took a daily oral antidepressant, so this measures the toxin as an add-on; the groups differed at baseline on one item (sensitive sensation) and the analysis adjusts for baseline; no confidence intervals, adverse events, sleep or quality-of-life outcome are reported anywhere in the paper.
notes: The abstract-only limits can now be replaced: what the abstract omitted is in the full text, and the real gaps are different ones. The add-on design and the absent per-foot result are the two that bear on how this trial is used elsewhere on the record.

page: botulinum-toxin-wheals
section: What is still unknown > the crossover to the untreated side
sentence_as_it_stands: A third of patients injected in one foot reported relief in both, and pooled analysis found no significant difference between one-foot and two-foot injection — which, if it held, would change the coverage arithmetic on this page by a factor of two. It rests on one trial's secondary observation and one rat model
quote: When comparing group D1 and D2, only hot sensation showed a significant difference; in other words, hot sensation improvement was significantly lower among those patients who received injection in both feet compared to one foot
corrected_wording: A third of patients injected in one foot reported relief in both, and pooled analysis found no significant difference between one-foot and two-foot injection — which, if it held, would change the coverage arithmetic on this page by a factor of two. It rests on one trial's secondary observation, a second trial's discussion, and several rat models: a three-arm randomised trial in 141 patients that gave every patient the same total, all in one foot in one arm and divided between both feet in the other, separated the arms on one of ten items — hot sensation, which improved less when the amount was spread across both feet — and its authors report the same bilateral relief after one-sided injection, without measuring the untreated foot. What none of this tests is a smaller total.
notes: Claim C008, which stays narrowed. The uncertainty flagged on the record is resolved: the bilateral arm's amount is a per-patient total divided between the feet, so a matched-total head-to-head exists, and the untreated foot was never scored separately.

page: botulinum-toxin-wheals
section: The coverage problem
sentence_as_it_stands: Which of those costs least in effect is not established by any trial, because none has varied them deliberately.
quote: When comparing group D1 and D2, only hot sensation showed a significant difference; in other words, hot sensation improvement was significantly lower among those patients who received injection in both feet compared to one foot
corrected_wording: Which of those costs least in effect is barely established: one randomised trial varied two of the three deliberately, holding the total per patient and the grid geometry fixed while comparing one foot against both — which halves the amount per point and doubles the area — and found the arms differed on one of ten items, hot sensation, favouring the concentrated single foot. The density of the grid has not been varied by anyone.
notes: Claim C002, narrowed → refuted. Taheri 2020 is randomised, double-blind and deliberate about exactly two of the three variables the sentence names.

page: botulinum-toxin-wheals
section: What is still unknown > covering a smaller area than the pain occupies
sentence_as_it_stands: Whether covering a smaller area than the pain occupies produces proportionally less relief, or none, is not established. This is the practical question the coverage problem turns on, and no trial has varied it deliberately.
quote: When comparing group D1 and D2, only hot sensation showed a significant difference; in other words, hot sensation improvement was significantly lower among those patients who received injection in both feet compared to one foot
corrected_wording: Whether covering a smaller area than the pain occupies produces proportionally less relief, or none, is not settled, but it has been varied once deliberately: in a three-arm randomised trial in painful diabetic polyneuropathy of both lower limbs, treating one foot at the full per-patient total was compared with dividing that total between both feet, and the two arms differed on one of ten items, hot sensation, which improved less under the wider, thinner coverage. What no trial has done is vary the fraction of a single painful region treated, or hold the amount per point constant while changing the area.
notes: Same claim C002, second sentence. The page's 'What would settle it' — a dose-and-area trial holding units constant and varying the fraction treated — is still unanswered, because this trial held the patient total constant and let the amount per point fall.

page: Pain biology, ion channels, and topical anesthetics for small fiber neuropathy
section: 3.4.3 The conformational change: how ligand binding physically opens the pore
sentence_as_it_stands: This rotation widens the pore from a closed diameter of ~1 Å (too small for ions) to an open diameter of ~10 Å (large enough for Ca²⁺ and Na⁺).
quote: In this study, we present molecular dynamics simulations of the open-activated pore-domain of TRPV1 in the presence of three cationic species: Na+, … Ca2+ and K+.
corrected_wording: This rotation widens the lower gate from a hydrophobic seal about 5 Å across when closed — narrow enough to block hydrated ions — to about 8 Å with capsaicin and about 9 Å when the channel is held fully open by resiniferatoxin with a spider toxin, which is wide enough for hydrated Na⁺ and Ca²⁺ (Cao 2013).
notes: The closed figure is wrong by about fivefold and the parenthesis is wrong in kind: at about 5 Å the gate is too narrow for a hydrated ion, not too narrow for an ion. The open figure is roughly right but belongs to the fully-open state produced by resiniferatoxin plus double-knot toxin; capsaicin alone, which is what this page is about, opens the gate less. Source: Cao E, Liao M, Cheng Y, Julius D, Nature 2013;504(7478):113–118, doi:10.1038/nature12823, section 'Opening of the lower gate' (PMC4023639). Darré 2015 — the paper on the record for this item — simulates the open state only and cannot supply either figure.

page: Pain biology, ion channels, and topical anesthetics for small fiber neuropathy
section: Part 13 Sources > What has no source, item 8
sentence_as_it_stands: The pore diameters of about 1 Å closed and 10 Å open in 3.4.3. Structural figures given without a structure paper attached.
quote: In this study, we present molecular dynamics simulations of the open-activated pore-domain of TRPV1 in the presence of three cationic species: Na+, … Ca2+ and K+.
corrected_wording: The pore diameters in 3.4.3 now have a structure paper attached, and the closed figure does not survive it: Cao 2013 (Nature 504:113–118, doi:10.1038/nature12823) measures the lower gate at about 5 Å closed, about 8 Å with capsaicin and about 9 Å fully open, by pore radii calculated from cryo-EM maps. The '10 Å open' figure is close to the fully-open measurement; the '1 Å closed' figure has no counterpart and should be corrected rather than sourced.
notes: This item can be closed once 3.4.3 is corrected. The molecular dynamics paper the record pointed at (Darré 2015) is the wrong candidate: it models the open-activated state only.

page: Pain biology, ion channels, and topical anesthetics for small fiber neuropathy
section: 3.4.3 The conformational change: how ligand binding physically opens the pore
sentence_as_it_stands: The S6 segments, which form the inner lining of the pore, rotate outward like an iris opening.
quote: conformational analysis of the pore in the presence of these ions reveals specific ion-mediated structural changes in the selectivity filter, which influences … the permeability properties of the TRPV1 channel.
corrected_wording: The S6 segments, which form the inner lining of the pore, swing outward — the side chain of a single isoleucine rotating away from the central axis is what unseals the gate — and TRPV1 has a second gate above it, at the selectivity filter, which rearranges as well when the channel opens fully. Capsaicin on its own opens the lower gate while leaving the filter unchanged, so the two gates can move separately; they appear to be allosterically coupled through the pore helix (Cao 2013). The S1–S4 domain, which moves in voltage-gated channels, stays still.
notes: Not wrong, but single-gated where the structural literature is dual-gated, and the distinction matters on this page because the capsaicin-bound state is the partially activated one. The simulation paper adds that the filter is unusually flexible and that its geometry changes with the ion passing through it, and that its authors never saw Ca²⁺ cross the filter in 1.6 µs, concluding that a further structural change must be required for calcium permeability (pp. 11–12) — a caveat on 3.4.4's calcium-influx picture.
